title: Orbital Glass — Vision Pro App Showcase
description: Floating rounded-rectangle tiles with translucent fills and layered drop shadows drift against a deep atmospheric gradient, each centering a 3D-rendered glyph — replicating the perceived depth of spatial operating system interfaces inside a flat slide.
philosophy: This template exists for the moment a speaker needs an audience to feel a platform, not just understand it. It borrows the visual language of spatial computing — translucency, soft shadow stacking, ambient light bleed — because those cues signal depth and dimensionality before a single word is read. It refuses flat fills, hard borders, and uniform tile sizing, treating each card as a suspended object rather than a grid cell. It is built for product reveals, OS keynotes, and app-category showcases where the interface itself is the argument.
goodFor: App platform category reveals with icon-driven navigation
Vision Pro or mixed-reality product keynotes
Feature suite showcases where each tile represents one pillar
Spatial OS or visionOS-style UI demonstrations
avoidFor: Chart-heavy quarterly financial reviews requiring data density
Dense bullet-point academic or policy briefings
Multi-column comparison tables with fine print
Brand style guides that demand strict 2D grid alignment
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like powering on a spatial operating system for the first time — weightless, luminous, and quietly theatrical. Frosted-glass tiles appear suspended at different focal distances, soft stacked shadows beneath each one implying ambient light drifting from above and behind. The overall mood is deep-space premium: sparse, unhurried, and dimensionally alive, with the hero tile commanding attention the way a flagship product shot commands a stage. Avoid any hard-edged flatness, uniform tile sizing, or symmetric arrangement that would flatten the sense of layered atmosphere.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with a dominant hero tile spanning cols 2–8, vertically centered with generous top and bottom breathing room against an edge-to-edge atmospheric gradient bleed. Two to three smaller orbiting tiles float at varying depths in cols 9–12 and partially behind the hero — staggered vertically to break symmetry and imply parallax. Title text anchors inside the hero tile, left-aligned with a thin rule-line separator dividing it from the subtitle. A minimal identity mark or deck label sits bottom-left in the outer margin; no header band.

examples.promptCore: Each tile reads as a frosted glass panel suspended above an atmospheric gradient — translucent fill, soft shadow stacking, and ambient light bleed implying genuine altitude above the surface. The composition breathes asymmetrically: one dominant card anchors visual gravity while smaller satellite tiles orbit it, each centered on a singular 3D-rendered glyph as its sole focal object. The mood is quietly premium and spatially aware — depth signals before words do. Avoid hard borders, flat fills, and uniform tile sizing that would collapse the perceived stack into a flat grid.

examples.layoutNotes: Asymmetric bento grid on a 12-column canvas with a generous outer margin on all sides and irregular inter-tile gutters that reinforce perceived depth. One dominant hero tile spans roughly half the horizontal space and full column height; three to four smaller satellite tiles fill the remainder with varied aspect ratios. Section label floats as ghost text in the upper-left margin rather than occupying a dedicated header band. Page number anchors bottom-right, outside the tile cluster entirely.
